result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a tight set, give every item a yardstick and flag the stale-cardholder and budget-phasing traps. B explains its comparison choices more fully (seasonality, uneven costs, a target for holds) and adds a useful caveat about branch hours. Its reason for dropping cost per visit is also sharper. A covers the money question a bit more through cost per visit, but its branch note is muddled, and B's renumbering of the original list is only a minor flaw. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick a similar, well-sized set, give each item a comparison basis, and explain what they leave off. A gives fuller reasons, such as cost per visit penalizing digital use and programs, and adds useful caveats about lumpy spending and branch hours, though its money side rests on the budget line alone. B covers money more evenly by adding cost per visit, but that measure comes with no caveat, and its branch advice is muddled ('all four branches in one line' versus system totals only).
